title: Search coverage is evidence about the search, not proof of historical origin

observed: The canonical queue keeps M-004, M-005, and M-006 unresolved pending exhaustive branch and history traversal.
Repository code search returned no indexed file match for M-004 in this run.
Recent commits contain downstream continuity records discussing M-004 through M-006.
inferred: A zero-result indexed code search cannot establish that an identifier never existed because index scope, branch coverage, deleted paths, and unreachable commits remain unproven.
A downstream commit mentioning an identifier is an occurrence record, not necessarily the immutable object that originally assigned it.
proposed: Every provenance reconciliation must retain a separate coverage envelope naming branches, refs, commit traversal method, search method, retrieval time, and known blind spots.
Promotion from unresolved to located requires exact identifier assignment plus namespace, owner, semantic-role, temporal-precedence, and immutable-locator agreement.
superseded: Treating the earliest returned search result as the historical origin.
Treating a zero-result code search as exhaustive absence.
Treating numeric suffix matches across unrelated namespaces as identity.
unresolved: The immutable originating objects for M-004, M-005, and M-006.
Complete branch, tag, deleted-path, and reachable-commit coverage.

durable_rule.rule: Occurrence, retrieval order, and search silence are each provenance leads. None becomes origin evidence without an explicit immutable assignment object and a retained coverage envelope.

excluded: personal, medical, financial, household, or relationship material

next_action: Obtain an authenticated exhaustive ref inventory and traverse every reachable commit and historical path for exact M-004, M-005, and M-006 assignment objects; preserve unresolved status when any coverage dimension is incomplete.
